title: Madhuri Dixit and Triptii Dimri Just Made a Film About a Dead Body in the Living Room. Netflix Dropped It Today.
excerpt: Maa Behen is Suresh Triveni's dark comedy about a mother and two daughters who discover that family bonds are tested hardest when the problem is lying on the carpet.
body:
Netflix released Maa Behen on June 4, and it is not the kind of Madhuri Dixit film most audiences were expecting. There are no dance sequences. No romance arcs. No sweeping emotional monologues set to A.R. Rahman orchestration. Instead, there is a dead body on the floor, a mother who has her own ideas about what to do with it, and two daughters who cannot agree on anything — including whether to call the police.

Directed by Suresh Triveni, who built a reputation for sharp, female-led storytelling with Tumhari Sulu and Jalsa, the film is a contained dark comedy that unfolds almost entirely within the walls of a single home. Madhuri Dixit plays Rekha, the matriarch. Triptii Dimri and Dharna Durgaa play her daughters, Jaya and Sushma. The setup sounds like it could be a stage play, and Triveni leans into that constraint rather than running from it.

A Body, A Problem, A Family

The premise is deceptively simple. A man turns up dead in the family home under circumstances that are not immediately clear. What follows is not a whodunit — the film is not particularly interested in the how or the who. It is interested in the what-now. How does a middle-class Indian family, steeped in the protocols of respectability and community standing, handle a situation that no amount of propriety can contain?

Rekha's instinct is containment. Jaya wants transparency. Sushma wants to pretend nothing happened. The triangle creates a pressure cooker that Triveni uses to surface everything the three women have never said to each other — about expectations, about sacrifices, about the quiet resentments that accumulate over decades of proximity.

Ravi Kishan plays a supporting role that reportedly adds a wildcard element to the domestic crisis, while Geetanjali Kulkarni, Arunoday Singh, and Shardul Bhardwaj round out a cast that feels deliberately modest. No distracting star cameos. No universe-building post-credit scenes.

Madhuri and Triptii: Separated by Three Decades, United by Instinct

The pairing of Madhuri Dixit and Triptii Dimri is the film's most inspired choice. Madhuri, who defined an era of Hindi cinema in the 1990s, has spent the last few years navigating a streaming-era career with mixed results. Her Netflix series The Fame Game (2022) was well-received but did not become the breakout hit the platform hoped for. Maa Behen gives her something that show did not: a director with a clear, specific vision for what her screen presence should do.

Triptii Dimri, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the most versatile actors in contemporary Hindi cinema. From Laila Majnu to Animal to Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3, she has demonstrated an ability to inhabit wildly different registers without losing her centre. In Maa Behen, she reportedly plays the daughter who most closely mirrors her mother — a dynamic that gives both performers room to work against type.

Why NRI Audiences Should Pay Attention

Dark comedies about Indian families are not new, but they remain rare at the scale Netflix operates at. For diaspora audiences who grew up with a specific image of what a Madhuri Dixit film looks like, Maa Behen is a deliberate subversion — and that is precisely its appeal. It belongs to a growing category of Indian streaming content that treats its audience as adults capable of handling moral ambiguity, tonal complexity, and stories where nobody is entirely right.

Suresh Triveni has proven he understands this audience. Jalsa, his 2022 film with Vidya Balan, tackled a hit-and-run with uncommon nuance. Maa Behen appears to bring the same sensibility to a story about family, complicity, and the lengths people will go to protect the people they love — even when protection looks a lot like concealment.

The film is streaming now on Netflix in Hindi with subtitles in English and multiple Indian languages.
